text: Body [AS. bodig , a body]: Ger. Körper ; Fr. corps ; Ital. corpo . The being which has its existence as an individual in space and time; the material thing. In physics, a body is a space-occupying being exercising certain forces. In mathematics, a body is simply filled space. In physiology and psychology the word is used to mark the contrast between mind and matter; Locke (e.g.) opposes 'spirit' to 'body' (in general), and we commonly speak of mind and body (the physical person). ( R.H.S. )
